overall: The AG found the Weston School Committee violated the Open Meeting Law by adopting insufficiently detailed executive session minutes for seven meetings, but found no violation for an unanticipated April 2018 executive session omitted from the notice.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged seven sets of executive session minutes, obtained through a public records request, were insufficiently detailed.
allegations.key_passage: We therefore find that the Committee violated the Open Meeting Law by failing to draft and approve accurate minutes for the executive sessions held on October 16, 2017; February 26, 2018; April 9, 2018; April 24, 2018; November 19, 2018; December 11, 2018; and May 7, 2019.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged an executive session at the April 9, 2018 meeting was held although the posted meeting notice listed no executive session item.
allegations.key_passage: Here, the Chair asserts, and we credit the Chair’s statement, that he was unaware of the developments in the litigation matter until just before the meeting.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law.

Re-create and approve minutes for the seven executive sessions (October 16, 2017; February 26, 2018; April 9, 2018; April 24, 2018; November 19, 2018; December 11, 2018; May 7, 2019) and certify to the AG within 60 days.
Each Committee member to view the AG's 5-minute training video on meeting minutes and certify to the AG within 60 days.
remedy_passage: In addition, we order the Committee to re-create and approve minutes for the executive sessions held on October 16, 2017; February 26, 2018; April 9, 2018; April 24, 2018; November 19, 2018; December 11, 2018; and May 7, 2019, and certify to this office within 60 days from the date of this letter that it has done so.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
